question.prompt:
The number of points common to the graphs of

\[ (x-y+2)(3x+y-4)=0 \]

and

\[ (x+y-2)(2x-5y+7)=0 \]

is:

solutions.explanation:
A product is zero exactly when at least one factor is zero. Thus the first graph consists of the lines \(y=x+2\) and \(y=4-3x\), while the second consists of \(y=2-x\) and \(5y=2x+7\).

Every common point must lie on one line from each graph. Substituting the first line's expression for \(y\) into the second line's equation gives the four possibilities:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x+2=2-x&\quad\Rightarrow\quad (x,y)=(0,2),\\
5(x+2)=2x+7&\quad\Rightarrow\quad (x,y)=(-1,1),\\
4-3x=2-x&\quad\Rightarrow\quad (x,y)=(1,1),\\
5(4-3x)=2x+7&\quad\Rightarrow\quad (x,y)=\left(\frac{13}{17},\frac{29}{17}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Each resulting linear equation has exactly one solution. These four points are distinct, and the four line pairs exhaust all ways a point can belong to both graphs. Therefore the number of common points is \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Intersect the component lines
